 Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (12-of-20 FGs), one rebound, seven assists, three steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 101-96 win over the Hornets on Tuesday.
 After scoring just 17 points in Tuesday’s win, which was a game he only played 29 minutes due to the lopsided score, Booker was able to get back on track in this one. He matched his season high for both steals and three-pointers in the win while also scoring at least 30 points for the fifth time this season. He has been excellent this season and will look to stay hot against the Lakers on Sunday to wrap up the week.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Devin Booker notched 17 points (6-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Clippers. 
 While Booker wasn’t as prolific scoring-wise as he was in Monday’s loss to the Spurs, the Suns didn’t need him to be. Phoenix’s bench was outstanding against the Clippers, with five reserves hitting double figures. The only issue for Booker on Tuesday was the four turnovers, but he’s been one of the few bright spots for the Suns this season. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Devin Booker amassed 32 points (10-of-17 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 The Spurs appeared to approach Monday’s game with the mindset that, while Booker can get his, they’ll make it nearly impossible for his teammates to contribute. He shot the ball at a high clip, but it’s tough to compete when no other Suns starter scores more than seven points. So far, Booker has slightly exceeded his ADP, and this should be another productive season for him individually. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Devin Booker finished Saturday’s win over the Rockets with 24 points (10-of-24 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers. 
 Counting Saturday, Booker has scored at least 20 points in five straight games. He needed 24 shots to score 24 points against the Rockets, but that tends to happen when Amen Thompson defends you for extended periods. Booker’s shooting 47.6 percent from the field for the season, and his current fantasy value aligns with his preseason top-30 ADP. The Suns begin a four-game week with a Monday/Tuesday back-to-back that begins with the Spurs. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday. 
 Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. He’ll continue to have the ball in his hands, and if he’s shooting the ball this well, the results will continue to be great for fantasy managers.

 #15 
 Devin Booker had 33 points (9-of-19 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), one rebound, two assists and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Booker was just 2-of-8 from behind the three-point line in this one, but made his hay at the foul line as he drained all 13 of his free throw attempts on his way to a 33-point game. The 30-year-old guard played almost 34 minutes despite fouling out for the second consecutive game. Booker and the Suns will be back on the floor Thursday at home against the Magic. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Devin Booker finished Monday’s loss to the Warriors with 26 points (8-of-18 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers. 
 Booker, who’s scored at least 20 points in four of Phoenix’s five games, fouled out with 57.6 seconds remaining and the Suns trailing by five. Phoenix did what it could to get one last chance to force overtime, but Collin Gillespie’s buzzer-beater attempt fell short. Booker has provided reliable fantasy value, but Phoenix’s schedule is the issue for fantasy managers. However, after playing two games in each of the first two weeks, the Suns play four games this week, counting Monday. 
 Devin Booker 
 PHX 
 Guard 
 #15 
 Devin Booker scored three points (1-of-7 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs) with two rebounds, seven assists and one steal in Monday’s loss to the Thunder. 
 It was clear from the opening tip that the Thunder wanted to make someone other than Booker beat them. The defensive strategy worked: Booker shot poorly, and the other Suns failed to do enough on either end of the floor to compensate. Even with Monday’s poor showing, Book has offered excellent category-league value through Phoenix’s first three games. He’ll look to bounce back on Friday against the Nuggets. 
 Devin Booker

 Devin Booker accounted for 43 points (17-of-25 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Warriors. 
 After scoring 23 points in the Suns’ season-opening loss to the Trail Blazers, Booker nearly doubled that output on Saturday. The Suns’ star guard shot 68 percent from the field and added strong rebounding and assist numbers. With the Suns playing just two games in Week 1, fantasy managers rostering Booker needed a night like this. The Suns have another bad schedule in Week 2, with only two games.

 Devin Booker finished Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers with 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one blocked shot. 
 The Suns got off to a brutal start on Wednesday, falling behind 17-0 and never truly challenging the Trail Blazers in Portland. Booker’s final stat line was decent, and fantasy managers won’t care much about the Suns’ 124-83 loss. Phoenix will look to bounce back on Saturday when they host the Warriors.

 The main thing we were watching was who was starting at center and Khaman got the nod tonight. Devin Booker will start at point guard which will be something to watch with how much he plays there. It will impact Collin Gillespie’s value as more of a streamer for 3-pointers.

 It has taken White some time to get going after missing the start of the year, and he’s still on a minutes restriction, but he was able to have his highest scoring performance of the season in this game.  Grant Williams made his season debut on Thursday and contributed 11 points (3-of-5 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns.
 Suiting up for the first time this season after missing the start of the year with a hamstring strain, Williams was able to make an impact immediately. Despite playing just 16 minutes, Williams was able to space the floor and score in double figures. They also outscored the Suns by 11 points when he was on the floor, which was the best mark on the team by far. Williams isn’t a standard-league option, but he is a solid depth piece for Charlotte.

 It has been a rough start to Anderson’s career, but he was able to get some offense going in this one. He set a new career high for scoring, and he has knocked down three triples in two straight games. One of the best shooters in the draft, it is good to see Anderson start to get things going on offense. He isn’t worth rostering in redraft leagues, but he is worth stashing in dynasty formats.

 Bones Hyland led the Timberwolves with 24 points (7-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, eight assists, two steals and five three-pointers in a 133-94 win over the Mavericks on Thursday.
 Hyland had his best game of the season in what ended up being a blowout win for Minnesota. He set season highs for both points and three-pointers while matching his season high for assists. Hyland has been a solid reserve for the Wolves this season, though the production hasn’t come consistently. Despite a fantastic performance, he isn’t worth adding in most formats due to a limited role.

 LaMelo Ball lit up the Mavericks with 22 points (8-of-14 FGs), three rebounds, nine assists, two steals and six three-pointers on Thursday.
 It wasn’t a monster game for LaMelo, but it didn’t need to be. He made the most of his 25 minutes on the court in the blowout win. This was his fifth straight game with at least 20 points, and he set a new season high for assists. LaMelo took some time to get going, but he is starting to get into a groove with Anthony Edwards sidelined. Minnesota has now won five straight games and will look to extend their streak with the Bulls coming to town on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Zaccharie Risacher led the Mavericks with 22 points (9-of-14 FGs), six rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in a 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves on Thursday.
 Risacher was the leading scorer for Dallas in this game, though most of his work came after the result had been decided. Risacher had a strong start to the season, specifically on the defensive end. However, he has cooled off a bit in recent weeks, though this was a nice outing for him. However, in the month of November, he has only scored in double figures in the games that were decided by at least 35 points, making him a difficult player to trust in fantasy basketball.
 -  Noah Rubin

 P.J. Washington finished with 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), three rebounds and one three-pointer against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
 Washington got off to a hot start to this game, scoring 10 points in the first quarter. Unfortunately, foul trouble limited him to just 16 minutes, and he didn’t score over the final three quarters. That pretty much sums this game up for Dallas, as they were outscored by 31 points after the first quarter. They were completely dominated in this game, though Washington was able to start off well, so that is something, I suppose. They’ll look to bounce back in Cleveland on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Trae Young led the Wizards with 37 points (8-of-23 FGs, 17-of-17 FTs), two rebounds, 14 assists and four three-pointers in a 144-140 loss to the Pistons in double overtime on Thursday.
 A big fourth quarter led to Trae setting a new season high for scoring. In fact, this was his first 30-point, 10-assist game as a Wizard and the 92nd of his career, which ranks fifth in NBA history. Unfortunately, after scoring his 33rd point at the buzzer with an incredible three-pointer to force overtime, he shot 0-of-7 from the floor in overtime, with the four extra points coming at the free throw line. Still, it was an excellent night for him and was certainly his best performance as a Wizard. It is also worth noting that AJ Dybantsa, despite a rough night, hit a tough mid-range shot to force the second overtime, which was a fun moment for the rookie.
 -  Noah Rubin
